speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members have spoken with passion about the challenges facing single unwed parents and their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members shared their concerns about how it is the innocent children who would suffer from their continued exclusion from society by discriminating against single unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We all agree that intact families are ideal, but as Members have previously raised, we live in an imperfect world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The single unwed is very often a victim of circumstance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In examining the inequality faced by a single unwed parent, Members, including myself, are not advocating for any extra assistance above and beyond what a couple receives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We merely ask that we not discriminate against a single unwed and his or her child, and that we treat them equally and with dignity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members have shared that a 2004 Cornell study concluded that children of single parents can do as well as children of dual parents, if the single parent is able to provide a sufficiently supportive environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Withholding support from an unwed parent could end up disadvantaging the child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Eight years ago, a Member asked, and I quote, "Is the Government looking at the unintended negative consequences that result from the policies affecting single unwed parents?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Are we examining the policies to see if there is an effect on the health, development and social mobility of the child?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Are we looking to see if inter-generational poverty is more likely to result?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do we care more about a set of stated principles or do we care more about the effects on our citizens?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the Government wants to discourage the incidence of single unwed parents, there are much better ways that do not have such negative consequences."  What about housing for single unweds?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Twenty-two years ago, another Member posed this question in this House, "Does it therefore become morally justifiable to deny an unwed mother and her child public housing, say, a rental flat?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If denied public rental flat, what is their choice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problem really is that unlike, say, London or New York, there is no large stock of affordable private housing for those who are deemed ineligible to qualify for public housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no real free market in the supply of public housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We therefore have to really be careful when we turn people out and ask ourselves where they will live." Twenty-two years later, I am glad that things have improved significantly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are significant steps forward to level the playing field.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this playing field remains unlevelled as, amongst several other issues, we have not resolved the issue of housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Single unweds and their children need a roof over their heads.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should look especially at single unwed parents under 35 years old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Those 35 years old or above can qualify for public housing under the Singles Scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their median salary has hardly changed over the years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to ask ourselves what options does a parent with a newborn and earning only $600 a month have?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They clearly cannot afford alternative housing options and they are then left with one last option, which is to stay with their family members.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with that and we all wish that it happens.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last month, I filed a Parliamentary Question asking the Minister for National Development whether HDB will, deciding not just on a case-by-case basis and without receiving an appeal, allow a single parent and his/her child to get an HDB rental flat when the duo cannot afford alternative housing options and will otherwise have to share a bedroom with existing family members in the family's home or stay in the living room because there is no spare room available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Happy that single parents with no other available options could qualify for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At my Meet-the-People Session (MPS) that evening, Mary, not her real name, came to see me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She is a single unwed with a five-year old child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Both her parents have passed on and she was staying with her daughter in the living room of her sister's flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was able to earn only about $300 a month as she had to look after her daughter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was told she and her daughter do not form a family nucleus and as such she did not qualify for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They did tell her that she can apply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But imagine the amount of anxiety a person desperate for a roof over their head faces when told that you are ineligible for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have sent HDB an appeal letter for her and I hope we will consider the appeal favourably.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) had previously said that "In relation to meeting the housing needs of children with single parents, a range of Government agencies work together to ensure that no child is without adequate housing, regardless of whether his or her parents are single or married".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that HDB has provided housing to single unweds under 35 years old and their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this is only on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We all understand the rationale of a case-by-case review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what we are doing is adding stress for people who already feel they are at the end of the road.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met Ema, not her real name, at my MPS last year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I met her, her daughter was only two months old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They were both living in a shelter when they came to me for help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ema is one of the most resilient persons I have met.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She is a living example of how housing has been a stress for all her life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From the age of five to 15, she grew up in a children’s home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was returned to her father for a short time before he disappeared from her life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She managed to stay with some relatives but eventually had to move out because of tensions that come with staying in a home that does not belong to you.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the age of 27, Ema had a child out of wedlock.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ema tried to apply for a rental flat and was told to see a Member of Parliament for help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She also got help from her social worker.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even her baby's doctor wrote a letter for her stating that, "As she (the baby) is currently staying in a shelter, she is frequently in contact with other residents who are unwell and hence predisposed to recurrent infection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, it will be greatly appreciated if the application for the HDB rental flat can be expedited." Ema did not shed a tear when she told me her story and I asked her why.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She told me that she no longer had any tears left.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was simply looking for a roof over her head and her baby's head.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appealed to HDB to allow her to rent a flat and I am glad the appeal was successful.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: HDB replied that, "We are pleased to inform you that we have obtained special approval for you to rent a 1-room flat with your daughter on compassionate grounds." I am glad the appeal was successful.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the whole process was extremely stressful for Ema who had a newborn, had no income, had no family members to help her, was living in a shelter, which made her baby sick frequently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And she had to seek help from three separate sources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Should cases like this not be a straightforward yes for a rental flat application rather than on a case-by-case basis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think single unweds and their children will also face a strong stigma attached to them when they can only get a roof over their heads through special approvals on compassionate grounds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that HDB should have enough data to identify clusters of people like Mary and Ema who undeniably need rental housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For other cases, we can still rely on a case-by-case review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But let us start by providing a sure "Yes" to those who we know definitely need our help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second request is about the language we use.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When single unwed parents do get approvals, I hope that HDB will no longer state that the decision was a "special approval" based on "compassionate grounds".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can we, like all other applications, simply state that their application has been approved?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third request is that we specifically state on the HDB website that a "Single unwed and his or her child" can apply, not guaranteed, but can apply for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fourth request is that our frontline officers be updated and no longer tell single unweds that they are ineligible for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, they tell them, like all other Singaporeans, they can apply if they meet the eligibility criteria stated on the website and HDB will assess their application like all other applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us make sure they do not feel discriminated against.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The other applicants were assessed to be able to stay with family members.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why then do we do this to single unwed parents?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this current housing policy does not prevent children being born out of wedlock.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the intent of the policy, but we really need to question whether it works.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have met a lot of single unweds and many did not plan to have a child out of wedlock.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was the heat of the moment and they got pregnant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the heat of the moment, just before they have sex, nobody would stop and think, "Wait if we do this and get pregnant and don't get married, we won't be able to get an HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let's not have sex." All of us sitting here know that this will not happen.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have a policy that will not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The only time when an unwed parent feels the impact of the policy is when he or she has a child and is looking for a roof over their heads.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The message that we are telling the single unweds is that they should get married.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But do we want to force a couple to get married so that they can get a roof over their heads?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What kind of a marriage would that be?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is this really in the best interest of the child?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is another way out for the single unwed, which is to get married and then file for a divorce subsequently and get sole care and control of the child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There was also no public uproar when we extended these benefits to single unweds and their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, there might be concerns that people will have a baby just to get an HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Honestly, while there might be some who would do this, Members of this House will agree with me that the vast majority of people will not have a child out of wedlock just to get an HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our policies should cater to the majority and we should not let the majority suffer because of what we feel the minority might do to game the system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the end of the day, we need to remember that there are children involved here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There might be arguments about what the single unwed should or should not have done and how they should face up and bear the consequences of their actions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the child is innocent and the child needs a roof over his or her head and the child needs a parent who is less stressed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Honestly, my wife is getting a bit worried as people now come up to me on the streets to ask if I am a single parent.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At a recent meeting with a social worker to discuss about help for single parents, the social worker was so sure that I was a single parent since I spoke up so much about this issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I do not need to be a single parent to understand the difficulties they face, the stigma they endure and the struggles they go through each and every day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Single unweds are not asking for more benefits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are asking that they and their child, all of whom are Singaporeans, be treated equally.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Three, update all our frontline officers that single unweds can apply for a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Being a single parent is twice the work, twice the stress and twice the tears, but also twice the hugs, twice the love and twice the pride.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am here to stand up for single parents and salute them for all that they are doing for their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope Members of this House will join me and us, and that our policies will continue to change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is 2019; it is time to level this playing field.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He has provided useful perspectives for us to factor in, in our continuous review of existing policies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In his speech, he has provided useful feedback on how our policies are implemented, and also shared the experiences faced by single unwed parents when applying for a flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I understand that there may be single unwed parents with us here today in the public gallery and I would like to unequivocally state in their presence that single unwed parents and their children are valued citizens in our society, and like all parents, they are respected for the love and care they provide for their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are no less a mother or a father, just because their child was born outside of marriage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Their children, like any other child in our society, are precious.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And every parent, regardless of their marital status, ought to be treated with respect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I acknowledge that in the past, the Government was fairly strict in limiting public housing access to married couples.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For single unwed parents, we hope to facilitate their efforts to build a stable environment for their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At MND, we recognise that having a roof over their heads is a key concern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are thus committed to ensuring that no child is left without adequate shelter to grow up in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I believe Mr Louis Ng can attest to the fact that most of the cases that he has shared with HDB have been helped by HDB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We believe home ownership provides long-term stability and progress for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why HDB reviews every application for public rental individually, to see whether the applicant can purchase a flat or stay with their family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This means working out each family’s housing budget and engaging them further to understand their situation, together with social workers if need be.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Such an individualised approach is taken for all public rental applications and not just for single unwed parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But we continue to take an individualised approach towards rental applications, as each of our applicants may have unique and complex backgrounds and circumstances, which would benefit from a more in-depth look.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng suggested that HDB should have some clear criteria for when single unwed parents can get a public rental flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Mr Louis Ng that there may be some common and objective factors we can identify, for example, income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But I would like to add that income is but one indicator of the needs of the applicant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We do not rely on a few predetermined metrics to understand the applicant’s circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are guidelines, and from HDB's perspective and experience, applicants can have more differences than similarities in their circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, the applicant could have medical conditions, which could impede his or her ability to live independently at the point of their application to HDB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This may be highlighted to HDB by the applicant’s social worker.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In such cases, once there is a new assessment by the social worker that the applicant is ready to live independently, HDB would proceed to allocate the applicant a rental flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, HDB does not apply a one-size-fits all policy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where appropriate, HDB will work closely with social workers to assess the best option for the applicant at that point in time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Next, I will touch on home ownership flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng has suggested a dedicated scheme to allow single unwed parents under 35 years old to buy a 2-room flat from HDB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The number of single unwed parents who apply to HDB for rental or purchase flats every year is not large.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We take a holistic approach for every application, as our concern is to safeguard the best interests of the child, especially in situations where the parent is single, young, not working or drawing a low, or perhaps irregular income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I want to assure Mr Louis Ng and Members of this House that HDB will not outright turn away any single unwed parent who approaches us to seek housing assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In every case, HDB will engage the parent to understand more about their circumstances, including their financial and family situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When purchasing or renting a flat of their own does seem to be the best arrangement for the parent and the child, HDB will support their application.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He emphasised that single unwed parents should not be made to feel discriminated against.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I wholeheartedly agree that we should review our communications and avoid unintentionally causing additional anxiety to single unwed parents who may already feel tremendously stressed by their circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have discussed this with the HDB Team, and there are a few things that we will do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we will review HDB's website to explicitly state that single unwed parents may approach HDB to apply to buy or rent an HDB flat, and how they can go about submitting their requests to HDB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope that these measures will help allay the anxieties from single unwed parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Single unwed parents and their children are our valued citizens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are committed to do better and to engage with them better.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am not sure if I have succeeded as much as I would like to have, but I feel that I have tried my hardest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I believe similarly that HDB's frontline staff do their best, but I suspect that the customer experience may not altogether be even.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Further, policies may not always be able to cater to every single citizen’s needs, which can result in frustration on both sides.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But there must always be empathy in our interactions and this works both ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I hope that when our citizens interact with HDB staff and officers, there is also mutual respect on both sides.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They have told me that they are committed to doing their work well and uphold high service standards.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Sun Xueling, under the Standing Order, the Adjournment Motion must end within 30 minutes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Lastly, I thank Mr Louis Ng for his suggestions and his work, and I hope that we can continue to work together to support our single unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.
